description: Attestation-based client authentication at the token endpoint: a client's attestation_* extended properties refused by the policy the token-endpoint filter and the OGNL criterion share (plan item S4c). The verified and refused decisions themselves are attestation.client.verified and attestation.client.refused, in the federation catalogue.

endpoint.description: Where the client's properties were read: token_endpoint_filter, issuance_criterion or startup_scan.

property.description: The name of the attestation_* extended property refused. Its value is never recorded.

enforcer.description: Which check refused the issued authorization_details: response_belt (the token endpoint's belt) or issuance_criterion (IssuedDetailsCriterion on an access-token mapping).

detail_types.description: The types of the authorization_details refused, comma-separated, at most eight. A detail's values are never recorded.

attestation.policy.invalid.description: A client's attestation_* extended property does not parse, holds more than one value, or would loosen the server's policy (the reason: unparsable, loosens, empty_intersection or foreign_htu), so the client is refused with 401 invalid_client. The start-up scan records each client once, when it is first found.

attestation.issued.refused.description: A token was refused because what it would carry is not held by the client attestation (plan item S4d): its authorization_details not within the attestation's (exceeds_ceiling), a question the model cannot answer (uncheckable), a token response too large for the belt to check (too_large), a refresh that must repeat its authorization_details (redecide_on_refresh), or a client with attestation_required that presented none (attestation_required). The belt answers the client 400 invalid_authorization_details (500 server_error for too_large); the criterion makes PingFederate answer with its Error Result.
